gadgets.sink: AllowOverride All on a writable document root: .htaccess is a configuration write, and a configuration write is a process
gadgets.payload: .htaccess containing  Options +ExecCGI  and  AddHandler cgi-script .<ext>  , plus a file with that extension, chmod 0755, whose first two lines are a Content-Type header and a blank line
gadgets.effect: escapes PHP entirely. disable_functions and open_basedir are PHP SAPI settings and do not apply to a process Apache execs through mod_cgi, so a setuid helper or any binary can be run when every PHP exec function is blocked.
gadgets.precondition: mod_cgi loaded, AllowOverride All (or at least Options FileInfo) on a directory you can write to
gadgets.trap: the script MUST print Content-Type and a blank line before anything else and MUST be 0755, or Apache answers an opaque 500 with the output discarded -- the same 500 a failed exec gives, so the two are indistinguishable from outside. Check the document root for a misspelled .htacess: it is inert, which both explains why overrides look disabled and leaves the real slot free. Remove the .htaccess afterwards; it enables CGI for the whole directory.

gadgets.sink: not the way in here -- a measured dead end worth not re-walking
gadgets.effect: execution really does happen: a missing binary answers 404 while a real one answers 500, which is 'premature end of script headers'. But a plain binary emits no CGI headers so the output is discarded, and query-string-to-argv did not fire on this build (an awk program passed that way left no file behind), so neither output nor arguments were reachable. Use the .htaccess route instead.
gadgets.trap: the 404-versus-500 difference is still a useful oracle for which binaries exist on the box
